questions.question: What is the primary purpose of digesting carbohydrates, proteins, and fats in our food?
options: To convert them directly into carbon dioxide inside the mouth
To break them down into smaller molecules that can be absorbed
To store them as large, unchanged molecules in the stomach lining
To allow them to pass through the digestive system without being absorbed

questions.question: How are absorbed nutrients transported to the cells where they are needed by the body?
options: They travel through the air passages of the lungs
They are carried through the body by the blood
They move along the nervous system pathways
They are pumped directly from the kidneys

questions.question: By what process do some nutrient molecules pass into the blood because they are small enough?
options: Active pumping
Osmosis of proteins
Diffusion
Filtration by the liver

questions.question: Which of the following is an adaptation of the small intestine lining that increases nutrient absorption?
options: A thick, smooth muscular layer that prevents molecules from escaping
A highly folded surface with tiny projections called villi
A highly acidic lining that quickly destroys large food particles
A completely waterproof barrier that only allows gases to pass

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the structure of a single bacterium?
options: It is a non-living particle containing only genetic material
It is a multicellular organism with specialized tissues
It is a microorganism made of a single living cell
It is a complex animal cell without a cell membrane

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding bacteria and human health?
options: All bacteria are harmful pathogens that cause infectious diseases
Some bacteria cause diseases, but many are harmless and some are helpful
Bacteria are entirely inert and have no effect on human health
All bacteria are helpful and none can cause disease in humans

questions.question: In which part of the human body do helpful bacteria live to assist with digestion?
options: The respiratory system
The circulatory system
The digestive system
The nervous system

questions.question: How do helpful bacteria in the human digestive system assist in digesting foods we cannot break down ourselves?
options: They release enzymes that digest these foods
They use mechanical teeth to chew the food particles
They produce strong mineral acids that dissolve the food
They absorb the food and transport it directly to our cells

questions.question: How do helpful digestive bacteria protect the body against invading pathogens?
options: By producing red blood cells to attack them
By competing against the pathogens
By lowering the body temperature to freeze them
By releasing antibodies into the bloodstream

questions.question: Which of the following describes mechanical digestion and where it occurs?
options: It involves enzymes breaking chemical bonds in the small intestine
It is the transport of nutrients through blood vessels in the liver
It involves the physical breaking of food, such as chewing in the mouth
It is the chemical breakdown of starch into sugar in the stomach

questions.question: What are the three major food groups that make up the solid nutrients we eat?
options: Vitamins, minerals, and water
Carbohydrates, proteins, and fats
Acids, alkalis, and enzymes
Fiber, glucose, and oxygen

questions.question: What is the function of enzymes during the chemical digestion of food?
options: They slow down digestion to allow better water absorption
They act as biological catalysts to speed up the chemical breakdown of food
They mechanically grind food in the stomach into a fine paste
They transport digested food molecules across the intestinal wall

questions.question: Into what smaller molecules are proteins digested by enzymes?
options: Starch and glucose
Fatty acids and glycerol
Amino acids
Water and mineral salts

questions.question: Which of the following large food molecules can be tested for using chemical reagents?
options: Carbon dioxide, oxygen, and water
Glucose, amino acids, and fatty acids
Protein, fat, and carbohydrates like starch
Saliva, bile, and gastric juices

questions.question: Which small food molecules, produced from breaking down starch, can be identified with chemical reagents?
options: Proteins
Sugars
Large fats
Insoluble minerals

questions.question: A student performs a food test and notices the reagent turns blue-black. Which nutrient is present?
options: Protein
Sugar
Starch
Fat

questions.question: What is the correct order of major organs that food passes through during digestion?
options: Mouth -> Stomach -> Small Intestine -> Large Intestine
Mouth -> Large Intestine -> Stomach -> Small Intestine
Stomach -> Mouth -> Small Intestine -> Large Intestine
Mouth -> Small Intestine -> Large Intestine -> Stomach

questions.question: How is the stomach adapted to perform its function in the digestive system?
options: It contains villi to absorb nutrients directly into the bloodstream
It has muscular walls to churn food and produces acid and enzymes
It is a long, highly folded tube designed primarily for water absorption
It uses teeth to grind food mechanically before it is swallowed

questions.question: What happens to food material that cannot be digested by the human body?
options: It is absorbed into the blood and exhaled from the lungs
It is converted into digestive enzymes by the pancreas
It is passed out of the body as faeces
It is permanently stored in the stomach to aid future digestion
